thread:
marta: Heads up - we started getting a flurry of latency alerts for text-generation p99 around 15:17 UTC. p99 jumped from ~180ms to ~950ms. Multiple customers DM'ing support.

neil: Any recent infra churn? deployments, kernel, firmware?

marta: infra change log shows a GPU firmware batch (FW-2.3.1 -> FW-2.4.0) rolled at 15:00 to us-east-1-gpupool-3. Also a CUDA driver bump to 515 on a subset earlier this morning.

ravi: pulling per-host p99 now. Early signal: spike concentrated on hosts updated with FW-2.4.0. Other hosts stable.

ops-bot: Incident severity: P2 -> Escalate if customer impact increases.

marta: can someone ssh an affected host and run quick checks?

sasha: on it. running:
```
uname -a
dmesg | tail -n 80
cat /proc/interrupts | sed -n '1,80p'
nvme list && nvme smart-log /dev/nvme0n1
iostat -x 1 5
/etc/init.d/checkpoint status || systemctl status checkpoint.service
```

sasha: dmesg frag: "nvme0n1: aborting command" and "nvme nvme0: controller reset due to I/O timeout". Also see PCIe AER warnings: "pcieport 0000:02:00.0: AER: Corrected error" around 15:02.

ravi: iostat snippet: 
"nvme0n1 0.00 0.00 120.00 2.00 4800.00 1024.00 41.50 12.30 89.60 0.28 92.10 0.40 98.50"

neil: avgqu-sz and await huge again. looks like device queue saturation. Could be PCIe link errors causing retries and higher latency.

marta: nvidia-bot: the firmware rollout included PCIe power management tweaks (link state changes) and new DMA descriptor handling. Could interact with NVMe driver.

nvidia-bot: Auto-ticket created: NV-INC-8421. Attach logs and host list.

ops-bot: Runbook suggests: 1) isolate affected hosts from scheduler 2) reduce NVMe queue depth 3) test alternate NVMe scheduler 4) open vendor SR.

neil: I'll execute isolation now - mark hosts draining in service discovery so new allocations avoid them.

deploy-bot: Marking us-east-1-gpupool-3 hosts as draining via service discovery.

sasha: trying non-invasive mitigations: lowered per-device nr_requests:
```
echo 32 > /sys/block/nvme0n1/queue/nr_requests
echo mq-deadline > /sys/block/nvme0n1/queue/scheduler || true
```

sasha: after dropping nr_requests -> 32 observed p99 on that host fall from ~950ms -> ~320ms within ~2 min. Customer errors dropped after drain. p95 stayed similar.

ravi: also toggled writeback settings for app cache filesystems to reduce synchronous bursts: 
```
mount -o remount,commit=5 /mnt/kvcache
sysctl -w vm.dirty_ratio=5
```

marta: good quick wins. we need reproducible repro in staging though. provisioning a staging cluster with FW-2.4.0 + driver 515 to run synthetic workload.

neil: proposed hypothesis: firmware change altered PCIe behavior (link retraining / AER) which increases I/O stalls to NVMe under heavy DMA from GPUs. Driver 515 may increase DMA concurrency, amplifying NVMe queueing.

sasha: I ran fio on host under light GPU workload and see increased tail latency when synthetic GPU process does large GPU->host mmap copies. FIO command we used: 
```
fio --name=randrw --filename=/dev/nvme0n1 --rw=randrw --bs=4k --ioengine=libaio --iodepth=64 --runtime=300 --numjobs=8 --group_reporting
```

ravi: nvme smart-log shows increasing media errors counter on some drives (media_error_count non-zero) but not widespread. capturing nvme-cli JSON to attach.

marta: open ticket to storage vendor with all nvme smart logs and kernel AER traces. SR-STG-5570 created.

ops-bot: Escalation rule triggered: contact vendor if p99 > 700ms across >3 hosts for >10m.

marta: Mitigations summary we've applied:
- Drained affected hosts from scheduler (no new tasks)
- Reduced /sys/block/*/queue/nr_requests to 32 on live hosts (improved tail)
- Set scheduler to mq-deadline on experiment hosts
- Staggered checkpoint/writeback windows for batch jobs (systemd slice with IOWeight=10)
- Added per-cgroup blkio throttle rules for background IO (cgroup v1 vh)

neil: longer term: consider firmware rollback for hosts where vendor confirms regression. Also add a preflight microbench step when rolling GPU firmware or drivers.

sasha: putting repro plan in staging:
- provision 10 hosts with FW-2.4.0 + driver 515 + kernel 5.19
- run combined workload: 60% token generation, periodic KV checkpoint writes, and fio randrw at iodepth=64
- collect dmesg, perf counters, PCIe AER stats, nvme smart logs

marta: I will notify support and affected customers with status update: mitigated by draining/route changes, engineering investigating.

neil: owners & ETA:
- sasha: complete staging repro and attach logs to NV and storage SRs (ETA 6h)
- ravi: vendor comms + gather nvme smart logs for all affected hosts (ETA 3h)
- marta: customer comms and runbook updates + add alert threshold (ETA 1h)

oncall-bot: Incident escalated to P1 after vendor SR opened and customer impact. Pager duty: @oncall.

marta: follow-ups: add a gating test to infra release pipeline: run a 30m nvme microbench under synthetic GPU DMA load on a canary host before allowing firmware/driver rollout beyond canary. Also document kernel options we changed.

neil: adding CI job and checklist item. We should also monitor PCIe AER counts as a signal during releases.

sasha: logging final note: while queue-depth reduction helps tail, it increases avg latency under very high concurrent IO. need to tune per-workload. We'll include performance matrix in postmortem.

marta: Thanks all. keeping thread open until SR replies and staging repro complete.
summary: p99 spike traced to interaction between GPU firmware update and NVMe I/O/PCIe AERs; mitigations: drain hosts, reduce nvme queue depth, change scheduler, throttle background IO; next steps: repro in staging, vendor SRs, add release preflight microbench
